message.content:
The title of “best” jazz vocalist is highly subjective and varies depending on personal taste, era, and style. However, several singers are frequently cited as the most influential and celebrated in the genre:

| Singer | Notable Contributions | Why They’re Often Considered the Best |
|--------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered a deeply emotional, conversational vocal style. | Her phrasing and emotional depth set a new standard for jazz singing. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” she had impeccable diction, perfect pitch, and an incredible range. | Her scat singing and flawless technique made her a benchmark for vocalists. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Possessed a rich, operatic voice with a wide range and impeccable control. | Her blend of jazz, blues, and pop showcased versatility and technical mastery. |
| **Nat King Cole** | Combined smooth baritone vocals with sophisticated arrangements. | His crossover appeal and lyrical phrasing influenced generations. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | Modern jazz vocalist who blends jazz with folk, blues, and world music. | Her innovative approach and unique timbre keep her at the forefront of contemporary jazz. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best,” it’s often a matter of which qualities—emotional expression, technical skill, innovation—you value most. Each of the singers above has left an indelible mark on jazz history.
